Claude Fable 5 is Anthropic’s generally available **Mythos-class** model: the same underlying weights as Claude Mythos 5, wrapped in safety classifiers and always-on adaptive thinking. Anthropic has not published parameter count, layer count, or transformer internals.[1][2]

## What “architecture” means here

Fable 5 is not a separately trained public model. It is one large language model with two deployments:

| Config | API ID | Difference |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Fable 5 | `claude-fable-5` | Classifiers can refuse or fall back |
| Claude Mythos 5 | `claude-mythos-5` | Same weights; classifiers off for approved Glasswing use |

Both launched June 9, 2026, with a 1M-token context window, up to 128k output tokens, and pricing of $10 / $50 per million input / output tokens.[2][1]

## Serving stack

**Always-on thinking.** You cannot disable thinking. Depth is controlled with the effort parameter. Raw chain-of-thought is never returned; `thinking.display` is `"omitted"` (empty block) or `"summarized"`.[1]

**Safety classifiers.** Separate models sit in front of Fable 5. They watch for cybersecurity, biology/chemistry, and distillation. Flagged traffic is handled by Claude Opus 4.8 (or refused). Anthropic says this hits under 5% of sessions on average, and more than 95% of sessions never fall back. Mythos 5 skips this path. Other interventions (prompt modification, steering vectors, PEFT) can limit effectiveness without swapping models; Anthropic estimates that path at about 0.03% of traffic.[3][2]

**Agent features at launch:** effort, task budgets, memory tool, code execution, programmatic tool calling, context editing / tool-result clearing, compaction, and vision.[1]

**Data path:** 30-day retention is required. These are Covered Models and are not offered with zero data retention.[2][1]

## How it is meant to run

The product design is long-horizon agency, not a chat-only stack. Official guidance is to run it in a harness such as Claude Code or Managed Agents: plan across stages, delegate to sub-agents, keep file-based memory, and check its own work over hours or days. Persistent notes helped more on long tasks than they did for Opus 4.8 in Anthropic’s tests.[4][2]

Example: Stripe reported a 50-million-line Ruby migration that Fable 5 finished in a day versus more than two months for a team.[2]

## What is not public

Anthropic’s system card describes Fable 5 and Mythos 5 as two configurations of one new model. It does not disclose mixture-of-experts layout, training compute, or parameter size. Claims about “persistent learning” beyond the memory tool and file notes are not in the official architecture docs.[5][1]
